subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module that constructs a swamp troll character with tusks, a mohawk, and bone fetishes in a Warcraft-inspired style, aiming to keep it around 400-600 lines using only well-documented API calls like createBuilder to minimize risk of errors since I can't test execution.

I'm mapping out which builder methods to use for the geometry—joints, chains, sweeps, lofts, parts, surfaces, decals, and spikes—along with painterly texture helpers like mottle, paint, and grain from the SDK to achieve a stylized, saturated Blizzard-esque look, while deciding to skip optional kits to reduce complexity and potential failure points.

Now I'm designing the troll's rig: roughly 2.2m tall with a hunched, big-headed stylized build. I'm placing the skeleton root at the hips around y=1.05, running a spine chain up through chest, neck, and head at y=2.0, then using inverse-kinematics limbs for legs down to foot targets near y=0.2 and arms reaching to hand targets around hip height in front of the body, all oriented with +Z as forward and +X as left.

Defining more chains...

Positioning the jaw joint under the head, roughly below and forward of the head's center, and sketching a simple box-based shape for it...

Now for the tusks, I'm mirroring a pair of curved spikes from the lower jaw front, symmetric around the center axis. For the eyes, I'm considering a decal or glowing plane with an SVG texture on the head.

Now I'm placing decals for glowing sepia-yellow eyes near the head's front surface, then moving on to lofting the torso with stations defining width and height at increasing heights up the body.

For the body, I'm attaching the loft to the spine bone, adding a belly lump, shoulder spheres, and a swept loincloth/skirt. For legs, I'm setting up limb geometry with a forward-bending knee joint and figuring out the hip placement point.

Now I'm checking the leg segment lengths against the hip-to-foot distance to make sure there's enough slack for a bent knee rather than a straight leg—segment lengths of 0.46 and 0.44 give slightly more than the 0.88 distance needed.

Setting up the leg chain with three joint points (hip, knee, ankle) parented to hips, then sweeping a tapered tube along it with thigh radius larger at the hip (around 0.085 down to 0.055) in skin color, and defining a box geometry for the foot.

For the arms, I'm positioning the shoulder at roughly [±0.36, 1.6, 0.03] and working out a hand target around [±0.4-0.45, 1.0-1.02, 0.4-0.45], using a limb helper with an elbow bend direction — still figuring out the right bend vector so the elbow angles forward-down naturally.

Now I'm setting up the arm chain with shoulder/elbow/wrist bones and fist spheres at the tips, plus thinking about chunky knuckle details. For the bone necklace, I'm planning small rod/capsule shapes hanging from the neck to represent dangling bone pendants.

Writing bone capsule function...

For the mohawk, I'm thinking of extruding a tall ridge-shaped blade running front to back along the head, defining its outline as a profile of points that taper from a wide base to a pointed crest.

Still writing extrusion outline...

I'll position it near the top of the head, and maybe add a second smaller fin behind it for richness, with stripe or grain paint patterns in warm tones. For skin, I'll use a mottled paint blend of moss green and dark green.

For moss, I'll scatter small cone spikes across the upper-facing body surface rather than risk a full card-texture system, keeping it simpler and safer. Warts get the same scatter-and-stick-sphere treatment on the head, and ears become extruded pointed shapes positioned outward on each side of the skull.

Working out the ear outline orientation...

Recomputing the cross product, I find using x=up and y=outward gives thinness along Z, which is correct for an ear shape facing outward from the head with height and outward extent as the two outline axes.

I'm defining the ear outline triangle with a base and a sharp tip point positioned up and outward, then setting its thickness, origin position, and planning the brow ridges, tusks, nose box, and eye decal texture with a yellow slit pupil.

For the eyes I'll make them glow orange using an SVG with an ellipse and narrow pupil, decide the glow effect isn't essential and skip it, then sort out materials and the decal call parameters for placement on the head part. I'm also planning chunky hands, feet, a belly loft, and sphere-based shoulder pads, while considering whether to add a back pack accessory.

Skipping a troll tattoo texture, I'm setting bone and tusk colors, then starting the actual module code. I'm importing the needed helper functions from the builder library and setting up scale constants like head radius, then beginning to define the skin paint material using a mottled, countershaded green-to-tan color scheme.

Continuing material definitions...

Now setting up the skeleton, starting with a hips root joint and building out the spine chain with curved control points.

Adding jaw joint and skull geometry...

Positioning the jaw joint in bone-local space, then adding two tusks as spikes anchored to the jaw bone near the front, with base coordinates placed symmetrically to match the jaw's width.

Now I'm adding ears bound to the head bone, and working out the mohawk geometry — it runs front-to-back along the head, thin in width and tall in height, so I'm computing the cross-section orientation and starting to define its outline points.

Adding small spike tufts on top of the mohawk, then starting a necklace loop made from a circular catmull curve positioned around the neck at the right height, sitting in the xz plane.

Writing bone-hanging helper function...

Adding skull detail with eye sockets, a hanging charm pouch, shoulder pad spheres attached to the spine bone, and starting the torso loft with stations at each spine point for width and height.

Still defining leg chains...

Positioning the foot box at the ankle joint so the bottom sits on the floor, then adding three small toe spheres spaced across the front and claw spikes jutting forward-down from each toe.

Now building the arm chain from shoulder to wrist with similar limb geometry, attached to the spine, and giving the hand a chunky box shape at the wrist tip instead of a sphere.

Next I'm sketching the loincloth as an extruded outline positioned near the hip, oriented so its thin dimension runs along the Z axis for a flat cloth look.

Now I'm figuring out how to scatter moss clumps across the torso surface using small upward-facing cones, filtering for upward-facing normals, and planning similar wart-like bumps on the head using the same surface-scatter approach.

For a swampier feel I'm considering hanging moss strands rendered as textured cards with a wavy SVG texture, oriented with a lean so they droop downward from upward-facing scatter points.

Writing frame array and texture SVGs...

Setting up the eye decal with mirroring for symmetry, naming side variables (L/R) based on sign of s, and wiring joint names like hipL/hipR and the shoulder pad bone reference to spine.joints[1].

For the torso, I'm passing the spine chain as the bone for proper bending, checking the joint count matches the path spans. I'm placing mohawk spike tufts along the head top, positioning their base slightly inside the mohawk silhouette with small radius and length, while skipping extra decorative runes for now and double-checking the head joint reference.

Now I'm verifying the neck joint count, the foot chain tip, and confirming the rng import is in place before finalizing the return of the root bone and starting the actual file with imports, metadata, and skin color definitions.

Defining paint colors...

Still writing bone charm geometry...

Checking that the torso loft near the collar and neck lines up with the necklace position, and that the hanging bones land around chest height in front — looks consistent. I'll also confirm the arm path target reaches toward the torso front at a reasonable height, then finalize the full code.
